cls: Ophthalmic antihistamine / mast-cell stabilizer (topical H1 antagonist)
quick: One drop in each eye twice daily (0.05% ophthalmic solution)
Use only if clearly needed; minimal systemic absorption
Ocular tolerance; avoid contact lens use while eye is red
summary: Epinastine hydrochloride 0.05% ophthalmic solution is a topical, selective H1-receptor antagonist that also stabilizes mast cells, indicated for the prevention of itching associated with allergic conjunctivitis. One drop is instilled in each eye twice daily throughout the allergen exposure period. Systemic absorption is very low. It must not be used to treat contact-lens-related irritation, and lenses should be removed before instillation.
indications: Prevention of itching associated with allergic conjunctivitis

dosage.d: One drop in each affected eye twice daily
dosage.n: Continue throughout the period of allergen exposure

admin: Instill one drop in each eye twice daily
Continue throughout the allergen exposure period (e.g., pollen season), even when symptoms are absent
Do not touch the dropper tip to the eye or any surface to avoid contamination
Remove contact lenses before instillation; do not wear lenses if the eye is red
Keep the bottle tightly closed when not in use
moa: Epinastine is a topically active, direct H1-receptor antagonist and an inhibitor of histamine release from mast cells, providing both immediate antihistamine and mast-cell-stabilizing effects in allergic conjunctivitis. It is selective for the H1 receptor but also has affinity for H2, alpha-1, alpha-2 and 5-HT2 receptors.

absolute: None per labeling (use only if hypersensitive to a component)
relative: Wearing contact lenses while the eye is red
monitor: Ocular tolerance and signs of contamination/infection

preg: Use during pregnancy only if clearly needed. Systemic absorption from ophthalmic dosing is very low (plasma concentrations ~0.04 ng/mL), so systemic fetal exposure is expected to be minimal.
lact: Caution is advised; given the very low systemic absorption with ocular use, clinically significant exposure of a breastfed infant is unlikely.
renal: No dose adjustment needed; systemic absorption is minimal.
hepatic: No dose adjustment needed; systemic absorption is minimal.

minor: Other ophthalmic drops (separate instillation by at least 5 minutes)

serious: Eye injury and vision loss from using a contaminated solution

monitoring: Ocular comfort and resolution of itching
Signs of eye infection (do not use a contaminated bottle)
counsel: Use one drop in each eye twice a day for the whole allergy season as directed
Do not let the dropper tip touch your eye or any surface
Take out contact lenses before using the drops and wait about 10 minutes before reinserting; do not wear lenses if your eye is red
Do not use these drops to treat irritation caused by contact lenses
Keep the bottle tightly closed and out of reach of children
pk: Antihistamine effect begins within minutes of instillation
Plasma peak ~0.04 ng/mL about 2 hours after dosing (very low systemic levels)
Store at 20-25 C (excursions 15-30 C); keep bottle tightly closed
pearls: FDA-approved ophthalmic agent - dual action: H1 antagonist plus mast-cell stabilizer, so it both relieves and prevents allergic itching
Not for contact-lens-related irritation; remove lenses before use and wait ~10 minutes before reinserting (benzalkonium chloride preservative is absorbed by soft lenses)
Very low systemic absorption makes systemic adverse effects and interactions minimal
Use throughout the allergen exposure season even when symptoms are absent for best prevention
missed: If you miss a dose, instill it when you remember. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular twice-daily schedule - do not use extra drops.
overdose: Overdose is unlikely with ocular use given minimal systemic absorption. Accidental ingestion of the bottle contents may cause drowsiness; manage supportively and contact a poison control center. Excess drops in the eye can be flushed with lukewarm water.
